thread:
olivia: FYI I rolled an INT8 weight-only profile (bnb/llm.int8) for rustle-7b with an interleaved layer-split optimization and we're seeing a weird sawtooth quality pattern across layers in the eval slice. anyone seen this before?

kai: Saw something like this once — usually an artifact of uneven group quant ranges or layerwise outliers. Got numbers?

olivia: Quick summary: longform summarization EM down ~2.3% and rouge-L -1.8 on the canary. Per-layer loss plot shows periodic spikes every 6 layers (approx). throughput +28% and latency -12% though.

raj: can you paste the quant flags you used?

olivia: Sure:
```
PYTHONPATH=. python -m bnb.ops.quantize_model \
  --model rustle-7b \
  --mode weight-only \
  --group-size 128 \
  --interleaved-split true \
  --per-layer-scale median
```

simone: interleaved-split is the new change vs the baseline?

olivia: yes — baseline was plain llm.int8 with group-size 128, no interleave. this interleaved split was an inbox suggestion to reduce kv-cache pressure.

kai: The periodicity (every 6 layers) makes me think of attention/ffn alternation — maybe group-size interacts with layer norm statistics. Do we have per-layer activation ranges?

olivia: Attached plot (pasted below) — activation std jumps align with the spikes. Also ran a quick probe where we keep first K layers in fp16: K=2 removes first spike, K=6 removes first two spikes but costs more tokens.

raj: Interesting. Two quick hypotheses: 1) interleaved-split changes how weight scales are computed across layer groups, introducing quantization bias at group boundaries. 2) some layers have heavy outlier columns; group-size 128 might be too big causing per-group scale collapse.

simone: For immediate mitigation we can: a) fallback first N layers to fp16 in the canary profile, b) reduce group-size to 64, or c) enable per-channel clipping/outlier mitigation. Which is fastest to test?

olivia: I spun up two parallel canaries: 1) group-size=64 (200 tokens of traffic), 2) first-4-layers-fp16 (same load). Results so far (30m): group-size=64 reduced EM delta to -0.9%, fp16-first-4 reduced to -0.5% but throughput dropped more.

eval-bot: perf-eval summary: canary-1 (gs=64): EM -0.9% | rouge-L -0.8 | throughput +20%
canary-2 (fp16-first-4): EM -0.5% | rouge-L -0.6 | throughput +12%

deploy-bot: Note: rollout paused for rustle-7b-int8-interleaved at 2001234500 by canary failure threshold.

kai: Given tradeoffs, fp16-first-4 is best for quality but cost heavier. Another idea: adaptive per-layer fallback — only layers with spike > X get fp16. We have tooling to generate per-layer delta table for that.

raj: Also try group-size=96 (middle ground) and per-channel clipping (top-k clip). That might remove outliers without full fp16.

olivia: I'll run a sweep: gs=96, per-channel-clip topk=5%, adaptive-fallback thresh=1.2 std. Plan: 3 canaries qps=200 each for 1h. Will post results.

simone: If sweep still shows sawtooth, we should open a small experiment to log quant scales at export time and compare with baseline to see if interleaving reordered quant groups incorrectly. Could be a bug in interleaved-split implementation.

olivia: Good call. I'll enable more verbose export logging and add a checksum diff between baseline and interleaved quant group boundaries.

kai: TL;DR: avoid full rollout. prefer conservative profile (fp16-first-4) until we understand group-level distortions. thanks for catching it early. :thumbsup:

olivia: +1, thanks all — posting results in this thread in ~90m.

eval-bot: scheduled evals: longform-summ, codegen-smoke, translation-slice — will emit CSV to /evals/rustle/int8_canaries/2001234567.csv
